name: Michael Grant / Captain KA’Zen
statement:
Dear Murals & More, Czech Village New Bohemia SSMID, and NewBo City Market Team, I am Michael Grant, professionally known as Captain KA’Zen — a multidisciplinary international artist, founder of Japofuturism, and creator of large-scale murals that honor community history while imagining new futures. I am excited to be considered for the NewBo City Market indoor mural. For over a decade, I have painted murals for schools, businesses, and community spaces that are meant to be lived with every day — welcoming, colorful, and full of story. My practice blends Japanese aesthetics with African heritage, ancestral memory, and spirituality to create Japofuturist worlds: figures who carry history and dream forward, landscapes that hold memory and possibility at once. NewBo City Market’s story — a place of gathering, food, makers, and community evolution — resonates deeply with my work. I am drawn to spaces where history is not frozen, but alive and evolving through the people who use them. If selected as a finalist, I would approach the design through listening: learning the Market’s history, the Czech Village / New Bohemia heritage, and the community’s hopes for the space, then translating that into an original, all-ages, inviting mural that feels both rooted and forward-looking. My portfolio includes YUME (The Dreamer), YUME 2.0 / The Dream Chaser, and Daughters of the Indigo Sun, alongside school and community murals that bring youth and neighbors into the creative process — including West Charlotte High 72' x 8' mural, Hydromer Inc. lobby mural, and Lexington, SC 89' x 11' panoramic mural. I am comfortable working at very large interior scale and delivering vibrant, durable work on schedule. Thank you for your consideration. I would be honored to create a mural that makes NewBo feel even more like home. Warmly, Michael Grant / Captain KA’Zen, Charlotte, NC | 704-756-3179 | InfamousKiddo47@gmail.com | Instagram: @captain_kazen47 | Linktree: AKcUracy | Applicant: Individual — Michael Grant / Captain KA’Zen

My work creates Japofuturist worlds where ancestral memory meets imagined futures. Through painting, murals, and mixed media, I bring Japanese aesthetics into conversation with African heritage, spirituality, and community story. I paint dreamers — figures who carry history in their skin and light in their gaze — and landscapes that hold both memory and possibility. Each mural is an invitation to belong: to see your own story reflected, to feel welcomed, and to imagine what comes next. Community history matters to me not as a static past, but as a living evolution. A market, a neighborhood, a school — these are places where generations gather, share, and grow. My murals honor that evolution with bold color, layered symbolism, and imagery that is suitable for all ages and meant to inspire every day. I believe public art should be both beautiful and generous: it should make a space more inviting, more memorable, and more connected to the people who use it.
